meta.title: Reversing Harlow's margin decline
meta.subtitle: Margin plan for the board, February 2027
meta.audience: Board of directors, presented by the CEO
meta.purpose: Approve the margin plan and the first actions

storyline.governing_thought: Fix promotions, delivery fees and weak stores now and cut hours last: that clears the covenant and reaches 2.7% by FY2028, and 3.0% with a second promotion wave

exec_summary.text: Wages are not the main cause: promotions, e-commerce and shrink explain 87% of the margin lost

sub_points.text: Labor rose only 0.3 percentage points of sales despite a 9.4% wage rise
38% of promotional events lost money; e-commerce loses about $10M a year

exec_summary.text: Management's 8% hours cut loses much of its saving to shrink; FY2028 profit stays near today's

sub_points.text: Leanest-staffed stores lose 3.1% of sales to shrink, the best-staffed 2.3%
Net of shrink and the wage rise, FY2028 operating income stays near $16M

exec_summary.text: Five moves on the real causes add about $22M a year by FY2028, led by store exits and promotions

sub_points.text: Promotions back to their FY2023 share add about $6M after lost volume; exits $6.6M
Six of the nine leases lapse by 2027, so only three exits need a board vote

exec_summary.text: With hours cut last, the plan clears the covenant and reaches 2.7% by FY2028; 3.0% needs more promotion cuts

sub_points.text: Operating income reaches about $38M after $7M of known cost increases
Cutting promotions to about 21% of sales reaches 3.0%; the stress case stops at 2.1%

next_steps.action: Cut the money-losing promotional events and reopen vendor-funding talks; keep depth in ValuMart trade areas
Roll out the $7.99 delivery fee and $100 threshold chain-wide; push for a flat rate at the delivery renewal
Vote on the three early store exits ($7.5M one-time) and give notice on the six leases ending by 2027
Restore receiving and produce rotation in the leanest stores; hold the hours cut until shrink there is at or below 2.4%
Decide on a second promotion wave, bringing promotions to about 21% of sales, if sales near ValuMart hold
Report the five gates to the board every quarter, starting with promotional share against 26.0%

sections.title: Why the labor cut is the wrong first move
Five moves on the real causes

lead_message.text: Promotions, e-commerce and shrink, not wages, explain 87% of the operating margin Harlow lost since FY2023

slides.rationale: What adds up to the change in margin -> waterfall
slides.unit_line: **Operating margin**, % of sales, FY2023 to FY2025; each step is the change in that line's share of sales

sidebar.caption: of the margin decline comes from promotions, e-commerce fulfillment and shrink
bullets: **Promotional mix:** 5 more percentage points of sales sold on promotion, each earning 14 percentage points less
**E-commerce fulfillment:** grew from 0.4% to 1.2% of sales as online orders nearly tripled
**Shrink:** up from 2.1% to 2.6% of sales, worst in the leanest-staffed stores
**Store labor:** only 0.3 percentage points, the smallest cost line that rose

footnotes: Promotional mix = change in share × 14 percentage points lower margin; private label = change in share × 12 percentage points higher. Part of the shrink rise reflects thinner staffing (p. 9)

lead_message.text: Fewer hours per sales dollar offset most of the 9.4% wage rise; labor cost grew just 0.3 percentage points of sales

slides.rationale: Three numbers that together size the wage effect -> kpi-big-numbers
slides.unit_line: **Store labor drivers**, change FY2023 to FY2025

items.caption: average hourly wage including benefits
items.relation: Management's diagnosis is right about the rate
drivers: Driven by the state minimum wage and a tight labor market

items.caption: labor hours per $1,000 of sales
items.relation: Stores already run leaner than in FY2023
drivers: From 7.02 to 6.60 hours per $1,000 of sales
Offset most of the higher hourly rate
In the leanest stores, receiving checks and produce rotation now get skipped on busy days

items.caption: change in store labor as a share of sales
items.relation: The net effect on margin is small
drivers: Labor cost rose $14.3M, the largest increase in dollars
But $9.8M of that simply followed sales growth

footnotes: Labor cost per sales dollar = hourly wage × hours per $1,000 of sales

lead_message.text: Promotions are buying volume at a loss: their share of sales rose to 29%, yet 38% of FY2025 events lost money

slides.rationale: Two clauses, one claim -> two panels

items.caption: of FY2025 events lost money after counting the extra units sold
drivers: Depth raised to hold traffic against ValuMart

items.caption: of markdowns paid by vendors, down from 55% in FY2023
drivers: Harlow now pays more of every markdown

footnotes: Post-event review of FY2025 promotions. The category team's point that the deepest-promotion stores grew comparable sales 1.8%, against 0.2%, shows volume, not profit

lead_message.text: Counted fully, e-commerce loses about $10M a year: the team's reported profit leaves out delivery and cannibalized sales

body.assumptions_header: Even on generous assumptions, the cut nets about $8.0M and fixes none of the bigger causes
assumptions: Shrink responds to hours as in FY2023–25, when hours per $1,000 of sales fell 6.0% and shrink rose 0.5 percentage points
Only fresh waste and receiving errors, 65% of shrink, respond to staffing; theft does not
Customer response to longer checkout waits and stock-outs is not counted, so this is a best case
E-commerce frozen at its FY2025 size, still losing about $10M a year; promotions unchanged

slides.so_what: The labor plan targets the smallest cause of the decline and gives back almost half its saving in shrink

body.assumptions_header: Less than half of the loss-making promotional volume has to go
assumptions: Loss-making events carried about 11 percentage points of sales (38% of events × 29.0%, if events are of similar size); this wave removes 5
Three-quarters of the removed sales are bought at regular price, gaining 14 percentage points; a quarter is lost at 6 cents a dollar
Promotional depth stays in the 11 ValuMart trade areas, where traffic is most at risk
Vendor funding, down from 55% to 46% of markdowns, is renegotiated but not counted

footnotes: Each point of promotional share left in place costs about $1.3M a year. The lost-volume share is our assumption: the pack has no lift data

Roll out the $7.99 fee and $100 threshold chain-wide

footnotes: Promotions and the delivery fee need no capital; of the sized moves, only the three early store exits use the $25M cap

body.assumptions_header: The labor step comes last and is netted for the shrink it causes
assumptions: Known cost increases: the 4% minimum-wage rise on FY2028 store labor ($6.8M) and the provider's proposed 3% ($0.3M)
Labor step: 8% fewer hours on the post-exit chain at 2027 wages saves $14.2M, less $6.1M of extra shrink
Prices, volumes and other costs held at FY2025 levels; FY2028 sales of $1,412M after exits and the fee change
Sales growth and vendor-funding recovery are upside not counted; cost trends other than the known increases are held flat, which flatters the base

footnotes: Formulas in the Calculations sheet of the source workbook

Team analysis of the Harlow briefing pack

constraints.item: Operating margin of at least 3.0% by FY2028
constraints.effect: base case reaches 2.68% ($37.8M against $42.4M); the governing thought, exec item 4 and slide 13 say 2.7% and name the second promotion wave that closes the gap

constraints.item: Lender covenant: operating income of at least $20M in FY2026
constraints.effect: FY2026 estimate $22.0M with promotions and fees from Q2; breaks if promotional share stays above 26.0% (gate 1, fallback: earlier hours cut)

constraints.item: At most $25M of one-time cost or capital FY2026–28
constraints.effect: only sized one-time cost is $7.5M for three early exits; private-label, shrink-control and six-store closure costs are not in the pack and must fit in the $17.5M left

constraints.item: No closure of a store with a lease beyond 2027 without a board vote
constraints.effect: three early exits are put to the board; keeping them costs $2.2M a year

constraints.item: Owners want to keep delivery in some form
constraints.effect: plan reprices delivery rather than closing it; each delivered order still costs $7.40 more than its fee
$6.8M cost in the full plan, $7.3M in management's plan; the hours cut saves 8% of the higher bill

constraints.item: Delivery provider's proposed 3% rate rise at the 2026 renewal
Shrink rises when store hours are cut
constraints.effect: management's $14.5M nets to about $8.0M; plan labor step nets $8.1M of $14.2M; the shrink lever uses the same 65% labor-sensitive share
promotions lever cut from $9.9M to $6.4M by assuming a quarter of removed volume is lost; independent review flagged the first version

alternatives.option: Management's plan: cut store hours 8% in FY2026 and freeze e-commerce
alternatives.why: safer for the FY2026 covenant but leaves FY2028 operating income near $15.7M (1.0%) because it ignores promotions, e-commerce and the weak stores

alternatives.option: Cut hours now, alongside promotions and the fee change
alternatives.why: FY2028 lands in the same place either way; cutting before the shrink controls work risks the full shrink response (stress: $9.4M instead of $6.1M) and service, and FY2026 already clears at $22.0M; kept as the covenant fallback in gate 1

alternatives.option: Exit only the six stores whose leases lapse by 2027 (no board vote, no exit cost)
alternatives.why: saves $7.5M once but gives up $2.2M a year; payback on the early exits is about 3.4 years

alternatives.option: Close home delivery and keep click-and-collect only
alternatives.why: conflicts with the owners' wish to keep delivery, and the pack has no evidence on how delivered customers would react beyond the fee test

failure_threshold.threshold: each point left in place costs about $1.3M a year; above 26.0% from FY2026 Q2 the covenant breaks; 3.0% in FY2028 needs share near 20.7%
failure_threshold.range: FY2028 margin low 2.1% (stress) / base 2.7% / high 3.0% with the second promotion wave and a flat delivery rate

consistency.headline: Fix promotions, delivery fees and weak stores now and cut hours last: that clears the covenant and reaches 2.7% by FY2028, and 3.0% with a second promotion wave
consistency.fix: after the review the base case fell from 2.98% to 2.68%; the governing thought, exec item 4 and slides 7, 11, 12 and 13 now say 2.7% and name the second promotion wave as the way to 3.0%

gap.base_case: $37.8M (2.7%) with every move including the labor step

closers.option: Second promotion wave: a further 3.3 percentage points of promotional share, within the loss-making volume, if ValuMart-area sales hold
Hold the delivery rate flat at the 2026 renewal instead of accepting +3%

closers.size: about $2.8M a year per 1% of sales

closers.option: Recover vendor funding toward the FY2023 level of 55% of markdowns

cases.base: FY2028 margin 2.7%, operating income $37.8M; 3.0% with the second promotion wave
cases.stress: 2.1% if promotions only return to 26.2%, private label grows at half pace and all shrink responds to staffing; still double FY2025 and above management's 1.0%

gates.threshold: at or below 26.0% from FY2026 Q2
gates.response: bring part of the hours cut forward in the best-staffed stores to protect the covenant

gates.metric: Comparable sales in ValuMart trade areas
gates.response: restore promotional depth there only and hold the second wave

gates.metric: Online sales after the fee change
Shrink in the two leanest quartiles
gates.when: FY2027 H2, before the hours cut

gates.metric: Chain shrink after the hours cut
gates.response: stop further cuts and restore receiving hours
